Subject: Hosting evaluation: tenancy choices, noisy-neighbor risk & SLA fallback

Hi Emma / Amit —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick call recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same frame:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary constraint: PHI + HIPAA compliance for certain workloads; some endpoints will see bursty clinical traffic (daily peaks around 7–10am ET).
- Desired SLO: 99.9% availability for inference under production load; p50 latency target ~120ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens).
- Architecture preference: Ember prefers a private/VPC option long term but would like a low-friction path to get there.

Options we discussed (short):
1) Hosted API (multi-tenant) — fastest to production, includes all redwood runtime optimizations (prefix caching, KV reuse). Good for non-PHI or low-risk routes.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool (single-tenant for your tenant), predictable throughput, can be set with strict autoscale policies. Good intermediate escape-hatch for peak bursts and noisy-neighbor avoidance.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full network isolation, KMS/HSM control, audit logs; recommended when PHI is involved and for ultimate control.

Key risks & mitigations (call notes)
- Noisy-neighbor: multi-tenant pools can see resource contention during sustained peak jobs. We mitigate with continuous batching limits, strict per-tenant concurrency quotas, and cross-tenant admission control. For strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
- SLOs: Hosted API provides best-effort latency SLOs in practice; for contractual 99.9% we typically pair Hosted with an autoscale-backed Dedicated fallback route to keep SLAs during incidents.
- Data residency & encryption: Private/VPC needed if you require tenant-managed KMS or on-prem storage of request payloads.

Proposed next steps
1) Ember to confirm: (a) daily peak QPS per route, (b) which routes will carry PHI, (c) retention/CBR needs.
2) We’ll send a short tenancy comparison sheet + a security questionnaire for your security team.
3) Proposal: start with a 2-week Dedicated PoC (small reserved pool for your account) to validate latency and noisy-neighbor behavior; if PoC passes, plan migration to Private for PHI routes.

Attachments: tenancy_comparison_sheet.pdf (short matrix), draft SOW template (we'll populate after PoC scope).

A few tactical questions for the PoC sizing: peak concurrent requests, average tokens per request, and whether you have a soft or hard latency SLO for tail percentiles (p95/p99).

Thanks — available Friday morning for a 30-min tech deep-dive.

—Markus

Thanks, Markus — very clear summary and appreciated.

Answers:
- Peak: our busiest endpoints (clinical-insight) hit ~260 qps during the morning window; sustained windows can last 45–90 minutes.
- Avg tokens: ~220 tokens/request (prompt + expected generation).
- SLOs: we can accept p50~120ms, p95 must be <= 600ms, p99 ideally < 1.2s for routed production traffic. For PHI routes we want contractual availability guarantees (99.9%+) and stronger auditability.

We'd like to pursue the 2-week Dedicated PoC you proposed — that seems like a good validation step before a heavier Private engagement.

I've attached our security questionnaire for your compliance team — it includes questions about data handling, key custody, and SOC 2 scope (file: ember_security_questionnaire.pdf).

Can we schedule the tech deep-dive for Friday 9am PT? Amit and I will join.

Best,

On Thu, Jul 15, 2027 at 10:12 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time today...

Emma — quick technical notes ahead of the Friday call and the proposed PoC. I'm a SE on the account and will lead the PoC engineering work.

Short answers to your requirements and how we'd operationalize them for a Dedicated PoC:
- Sizing: for 260 qps @ ~220 tokens and want p95 <= 600ms, a small dedicated pool of 4x A100-equivalent workers with batching window tuned to 20–30ms should be a safe start. We'll run load tests to validate.
- Noisy neighbor controls: in Dedicated pools we allocate GPU workers exclusively to your tenancy; for Hosted we use token- and concurrency-level admission control, tenant-aware queueing, and per-tenant burst caps.
- Fallback/escape hatch: configure routing policy so production traffic hits Hosted for day-to-day, but spikes auto-route to Dedicated (priority + canary weighting) — this maintains cost efficiency while protecting SLOs. We can formalize as: primary: Hosted -> fallback: Dedicated (route-level policy).
- Observability: we'll instrument per-route token-level latency, GPU utilization, queue depth, and KV cache hit rate. We'll provide a dashboard and a 30-day audit log for PoC.

Proposed PoC scope (deliverables):
- 2-week dedicated pool deployment + load-testing script (we'll run with Ember's test tokens).
- Observable dashboards + alerting for p95/p99 and availability.
- Run two noisy-neighbor fault injection tests (simulated cross-tenant heavy batches) and measure tail latency.
- Security/Compliance review with your security team (we'll fill out the questionnaire and return).

I attached a short SOW draft to capture timeline and acceptance criteria: sow_draft_v1.docx. We'll also link the HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/records/EMB-042

If that scope looks good we'll send a PoC order (no long-term commitment) and schedule the infra kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to Friday.

—Ben
